# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which states: "Cut the white wire." 

However, I cannot see the bomb to know which wire is white, nor can I speak. Deaf can see the bomb and its wire colors, and Deaf can speak aloud so that I can hear. Since "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something," sending gestures before Deaf establishes a protocol risks misinterpretation. 

I must wait for Deaf to view the bomb and speak to establish a code (e.g., assigning specific gestures to each wire color or position), after which I can signal the correct choice using the agreed gesture.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Bomb status: 1) Strip has 3 engraved symbols: upside-down capital T, looped square / four-corner knot symbol, upside-down capital T. 2) Keypad has 4 slots: slot 1 is 2, slot 2 is 9, slot 3 is 0, slot 4 is 8. Keypad requires 1 digit. 3) There are 6 wires (positions 1 to 6). 4) Display and Light are present but unreadable by touch. Please gesture instructions to Deaf so Deaf can speak the required action to me.
Deaf says: BOMB STATE: DISPLAY has [6]. LIGHT is [red]. STRIP is [blue, yellow, blue]. KEYPAD has 4 buttons: 1:[2], 2:[9], 3:[0], 4:[8], requires 1 digit, currently entered nothing. WIRES has 6 wires: 1: blue, 2: white, 3: red, 4: purple, 5: orange, 6: green. Mute, please gesture the solution/instructions to me, and I will speak them to Blind.

The manual instructs to cut the white wire. According to Deaf, wire 2 is white ("WIRES has 6 wires: 1: blue, 2: white..."). 

I will gesture `✌` (two fingers / number 2 / scissors) to Deaf so Deaf can identify wire 2 / cutting and instruct Blind accordingly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute gestured 2 (peace sign / two fingers). If you asked Mute a question or need an index/number, the answer is 2. Context from bomb: Wire 2 is white. Keypad button 1 is engraved 2, button 2 is engraved 9. Display shows 6. Light is currently yellow.

I have already communicated the index corresponding to the white wire (`✌` for wire 2) to Deaf, who relayed that wire 2 is white to Blind at the end of Turn 2. Since Blind acts immediately after me this turn, I will wait to see Blind's action or response.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf told me you gestured 2 (peace sign), but I cannot act yet because a wrong action detonates the bomb, and I do not know whether 2 means: 1) Cut wire 2, 2) Press keypad slot 2 (which is digit 9), or 3) Press keypad slot 1 (which is digit 2). Please reply to Deaf using this exact two-gesture sequence: First gesture indicates the module: use 🤏 (pinch) for CUT WIRE, or use 👉 (pointing right) for PRESS KEYPAD SLOT. Second gesture indicates the exact 1-based index: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 🖐 for 5, etc. Deaf will report your gestures to me and I will perform the action.
Deaf says: UPDATE: DISPLAY has changed to [1]. LIGHT has changed to [blue]. STRIP is still [blue, yellow, blue]. KEYPAD is still 1:[2] 2:[9] 3:[0] 4:[8] (needs 1 digit, entered nothing). WIRES: 1:blue, 2:white, 3:red, 4:purple, 5:orange, 6:green.

Blind requested a specific two-gesture code:
1. `🤏` for "CUT WIRE"
2. `✌` for index 2 (the white wire at position 2)

I will send this gesture sequence to Deaf so Deaf can relay the instruction clearly to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: UPDATE: DISPLAY is now [7], LIGHT is now [green]. Mute gestured to me: [pinching hand 🤏, then two fingers ✌]. Blind, this might mean press button 2 (which has label 9) or press the button with digit 2 (which is button 1), or pinch/cut wire 2. Wire 2 is white. Keypad button 1 is engraved 2, button 2 is engraved 9.

I have already sent the two-gesture sequence requested by Blind (`🤏` for cutting a wire, followed by `✌` for wire index 2). Deaf relayed this exact sequence to Blind at the end of the previous round. Blind now has the complete instruction and acts immediately after me this round.

```
wait()
```
